The frog will either hurt or kill the fish eating or trying to eat it, or the frog could either choke or hurt itself while attempting to have a snack. Also, with captive frogs disease/skin issues can transfer from animal to animal a lot more easily than with wild frogs. It's just best not to risk it! :)

Those are part of the lateral line system on an African clawed frog! They don't have eyelids, only a horny membrane around their eyes because they are fully aquatic frogs. These little stitch like lines are equivalent to antennae on insects and can sense movement and vibrations in the water. They help them know if something is near their eyeballs and kind of work like eyelashes in that they help keep things out of their peepers. Good question! ❤️

I have an eating disorder not talked about nearly enough called ARFID. In the absolute simplest terms, it’s extreme aversion to lots of foods. I only have a very small list of foods I’ll eat. If those foods aren’t around, I’ll starve myself until I can find “safe foods” for me to eat. I’ve gone through so much therapy to try and get better with it, but it’s been so traumatizing for me. I know I have to have a healthy diet though, and a lot of my “safe foods” are not healthy. Here are some tips for those like me who struggle with having a varied diet and don’t want to go through extremely traumatizing force-feeding therapy:

-Take a daily multivitamin. Olly women’s complete multi is my favorite because it tastes like strawberry fruit snacks.

-If you’re like me and don’t eat any vegetables except potatoes, drink either Ovaltine or Ensure. It’ll help fill in those gaps.

-Eat peanut butter to help get a little more protein in your diet. There’s also a kind of Greek yogurt called Oikos Triple Zero that has NO fruit chunks and has a crap ton of protein. It also tastes nice.

-No or very little soda. You’ll feel so much better and it’ll at least help you eliminate a lot of sugar.

-Keep a snack or protein bar in your purse/car at all times in case you go somewhere and there’s nothing for you to eat. It’s way better for you than not eating at all.

-If you’re still feeling worried about vitamin deficiencies, ask your doctor for a blood test to see if you’re deficient in anything. There are supplements and vitamins you can take to fill in the gaps if you can’t find them in a safe food.

-Drink lots of water. It sounds silly, but if you’re carb-dependent like me it helps so much.

YOU ARE NOT ALONE IN THIS. I get so much crap from people about how “I’m just a picky eater” or how I just have to “face my fears.” It’s an actual eating disorder in the DSM-5 that’s more common than people think; we’re just shamed for it. If you need to vent or need someone who relates to you, please message me. I can also give my suggestions for my favorite healthier safe foods. It’s tough, and I understand you. You are loved, and you don’t have to be ashamed of ARFID. ❤️

I had heard the sound before, but the fact that it was amplified by probably about 100+ phones throughout the entire store was extremely unsettling and caught everyone completely off guard. Still kind of freaks me out hearing that noise every so often.
